newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Hi-techs busy as stocks rally.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Hi-techs busy as stocks rally.

text.p: Technology stocks are stepping back into the limelight they stepped out of a couple weeks ago and options activity is keeping up with the renewed interest in the shares.
On Tuesday, as the Nasdaq 100 index .NDX closed in on an all-time high, options on technology stocks topped the actives lists at most of the options exchanges.
On the Pacific Exchange, which trades a large number of technology options, Compaq Computer Corp, Micron Technology Inc and Sun Microsystems Inc were among the busiest options.
The Compaq July 105 call was the most active option, with late session volume of more than 11,600 contracts.
Underlying shares of the computer maker were up four at 109-1/8 on about 5.2 million shares in consolidated trading.
Options on another computer maker, Dell Computer Corp, were busy at the Philadelphia Stock Exchange as that stock climbed 4-1/2 to 119-7/8 on nearly eight million shares.
Among Dell options, the June 120 call traded 3,835 contracts, the June 115 call traded 2,530 and the July 120 call traded nearly 1,500.
The most active Dell put was the June 110, which traded about 1,670 contracts.
As for the NDX, which is made up of 100 of the largest non-financial securities listed on the Nasdaq stock market, it ended up 13.50 points, or 1.4 percent, at a record 989.37.
Most of the NDX options activity was in the June series ahead of their expiration at the end of the week.
The June 990 calls traded 3,650 contracts and the June 970 calls traded about 1,270.
"It looks like there's no clear top in sight," Brian Belski at Dain Bosworth said of the NDX chart.
Jesse Stamer, general partner at TradeNet LP, a designated primary market maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, said the NDX would likely reach the 1,000 level before pausing.
"It's looking like it's going to push toward that benchmark millennium," he said. "It looks very powerful."
He added that the index held fairly steady even as the broad S&P 500 .SPX backed off its record high.
The NDX's previous an all-time intraday high, hit on May 28, was 988.40. On Tuesday it reached 991.85 intraday.
Belski said support on a correction should emerge around the 950 level and that 900 was critical longer-term support.
"If that would break, it would reverse this longer-term uptrend," he said.
Stamer said most of the options activity he has observed has been from call sellers.
"What I see mostly is that people are offering calls to increase their yield," he explained. "So they're doing buy-writes.
"They already own the indexes and they're offering calls to increase yield," he said.
